lock screen and recent apps need the accessibility service, which is off
● on: lock screen and recent apps work

Android lets an app lock the screen or show recent apps only through an accessibility service. OmaLauncher++ has one that does just that: when you make a gesture set to lock the screen or to recent apps, it asks Android to, as the power button or the recents button would.

It asks Android for no events and can\'t read what\'s on the screen or what you type. Android will warn that accessibility services can see and control your screen: that\'s what a service could ask for, not what this one does. It stays off until you turn it on, and you can turn it off there any time.

To turn it on, open accessibility settings, find OmaLauncher++ gestures among the installed apps, and switch it on. If Android says it\'s a restricted setting, open app info, tap ⋮, allow restricted settings, and try again.
Lets home\'s gestures lock the screen and show recent apps, and nothing else. It reads nothing on the screen and sees nothing you type.
